evals.name: missing-inputs
evals.prompt: Write the docs page for the new replay feature. That's all I have. How do you proceed? Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Establish required inputs first: owning repository and destination page, document type, reader and outcome, authoritative product source for every API/command/version/capability, scope and exclusions. Resolve routine details from repository evidence; ask only when materially different types, audiences or product choices remain plausible.
assertions: Lists the inputs to establish before drafting: owning repository and destination, document type, target reader and outcome, authoritative product source, and scope.
Says to use repository evidence to resolve routine details and ask only when materially different choices remain plausible.
Says a product or API claim without first-party source evidence stops the drafting of that claim rather than being guessed.

evals.name: unprovable-claim-and-translation
evals.prompt: The page needs a TypeScript version of a C# example that registers a reactor. I don't have the TypeScript client source open, but I'm pretty sure the API mirrors C#. The build also passes. Should I translate it and ship? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: No. Never translate a C# example into another client language by guess; verify each API and command against first-party source at the applicable revision (via cratis-technical-examples). A passing build proves rendering, not technical correctness; omit the claim or mark the gap for the maintainer.
assertions: Says not to translate a C# example into another client language by guess.
Says every API and command must be verified against first-party source at the applicable revision, using the technical-examples skill.
Says a successful build proves rendering, not technical correctness.
Says to omit the claim or mark the gap for the owning maintainer when the source cannot prove it.

evals.name: scope-and-output
evals.prompt: While drafting the how-to page, I notice the sidebar navigation is missing the entry and a synced copy of the page in the site repo has a typo. Should I fix both while I'm there? What do I deliver at the end? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Stay within content. Do not modify navigation or generated/synchronized copies; placement and navigation belong to the owning repository's workflows, and an existing page's authored source is edited, never a synced copy. Deliver page content only at the approved destination and report the authoritative source checked and remaining verification.
assertions: Says not to wire navigation because this skill owns content, not placement or navigation.
Says never to patch a synchronized copy; find the authored source instead.
Says to return or write the page content only at the already approved destination.
Says to report the authoritative source checked and the verification that remains.

evals.name: document-type-shapes
evals.prompt: I have to deliver four pages on projections: a first-time guided build, a fix for a stuck rebuild, a page on why projections are eventually consistent, and a lookup of every attribute. Map each to a document type and its shape. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Tutorial (ordered steps with visible results), how-to (prerequisites, direct procedure, completion check), explanation (concepts, boundaries, trade-offs, diagram), reference (exhaustive tables, fields, commands, signatures).
assertions: Maps the guided first build to a tutorial with ordered steps and visible results.
Maps the stuck rebuild fix to a how-to with prerequisites, a direct procedure and a completion check.
Maps the eventual-consistency page to an explanation with concepts, boundaries, trade-offs and a diagram.
Maps the attribute lookup to a reference with exhaustive tables or fields.
